expectations.text: Rejects the 'renderer is leaking' / 'cache or teardown bug' framing and identifies the per-poster texture SIZE as the root cause
expectations.evidence: rejects renderer-leak; per-poster texture SIZE is root cause

expectations.text: Explains a decoded image costs width*height*4 bytes at the source image's resolution regardless of the display box, so a 2000x3000 master is ~24 MB whether or not it's shown small
expectations.evidence: decoded image = w*h*4 at source res regardless of draw box (~24MB)

expectations.text: Explains that enlarging the LRU cache makes the OOM worse/sooner because each cached entry is a full-size texture, not that it helps
expectations.evidence: 500-entry LRU of 24MB masters = ~12GB ceiling; bump made OOM sooner

expectations.text: Fix requests a cell-sized rendition from the image service (?w=/?h=) instead of the master URL
expectations.evidence: renditionUrl() ?w=300&h=450 quantized ladder instead of master

expectations.text: References a concrete low-end-TV texture/RAM budget (tens of MB for textures, ~1 GB shared RAM) rather than treating memory as ample
